statement: The 2002/2003 Biskup-Chayes nearest-neighbor mean-field theorem supplies discontinuity for q=3 only in sufficiently large dimension; its abstract does not supply the universal d>=3 conclusion.

source.quote: provided the dimension is sufficiently large

statement: On S={x_i>=0,sum x_i=1} with F_J(x)=sum x_i log x_i-(J/2)sum x_i^2 and J0=4 log 2, the global minimizers are u=(1/3,1/3,1/3) and the permutations of v=(2/3,1/6,1/6). The minimum over continuous paths u to v of max(F_J0-min F_J0) equals Delta=log 3-(19/12)log 2>0, attained at s=(1/2,1/4,1/4) along the symmetric path.
assumptions: continuous paths in the full simplex
proof_or_counterexample: Complete independent analytic proof in ATTEMPT.md: classify interior stationary points; rule out boundary minima; use a strictly convex x1=1/2 separating section for the minimax lower bound and an explicit path for equality.
remaining_gap: No analytic gap identified in this auxiliary proof; independent review and novelty check pending. Parent lattice problem remains unproved.

statement: For the same F,J0,u,v, the epsilon approximate-minimizer sublevel at J0 contains a continuous path u to v iff epsilon>=Delta. For every epsilon>Delta and any 0<h<min(J0,3(epsilon-Delta)), a linear interpolation x(m(J)) across [J0-h,J0+h] satisfies F_J(x(m(J)))-min F_J<=Delta+abs(J-J0)/3<epsilon continuously.
proof_or_counterexample: Explicit continuous approximate-minimizer counterexample to a jump conclusion from this inequality alone; norm squares on the simplex lie in [1/3,1], giving the coupling-perturbation allowance abs(J-J0)/3.
remaining_gap: This vector selection is not asserted to be a lattice Gibbs magnetization. A lattice jump still needs sharper bounds and Gibbs-state arguments.

statement: For the Biskup-Chayes Main Theorem (1.12) in its Potts normalization, q=3 has n=2,kappa=2/3 and error allowance E_d(J0)=(2J0/3)I_d>=4 log 2/(3d), since I_d>=1/(2d). At d=3 this allowance is at least 0.3080654135821979, or 272.804653325636 times Delta. The necessary condition E_d(J0)<Delta cannot hold for d<=818. Passing the lower-bound condition at d=819 is not sufficient.
assumptions: the cited rescaled spin inner product

source.locator: equations (1.12),(1.13),(2.3),(2.7); proof of Theorem 2.1, delta_d=(q-1)^2 I_d/(2q)

proof_or_counterexample: Pair k with k+(pi,...,pi) to obtain integral a^2/(1-a^2)>=integral a^2=1/(2d). The integer inequality 3^(12d)>2^(19d+16) fails at 818 and holds at 819; check_barrier.py verifies the exact integers and reports decimal measurements.
remaining_gap: An allowance is not the actual Gibbs approximation error. This blocks only the stated coarse barrier criterion, not C0048 or other methods.

statement: The cited Biskup-Chayes Theorem 2.1 supplies a jump at J_t near J_MF in large dimension but explicitly does not establish m_*(J)=0 for all J<J_t. It alone therefore does not identify J_t with the first critical point J_c, which is needed to match C0048's critical-magnetization definition.
assumptions: use of the exact conclusion of the cited Theorem 2.1
C0048 interpreted by the PIMS critical spontaneous-magnetization definition

source.locator: Theorem 2.1 and following paragraph, printed pp. 63-64
source.quote: does not permit us to conclude

proof_or_counterexample: Source-scope audit: a jump at some J_t>=J_c does not imply a jump at J_c without identifying the two points.
remaining_gap: Does not assess other large-d theorems; current openness remains UNKNOWN.

statement: On the physical path -1--0--1--2 with its two endpoints wired, at q=3,p=1/2 the ordinary 0-to-2 path probability is 1/11 whereas wired-component connectivity is 7/22. For A1=the left edge open and A2=at least one of the two right edges open, P(A1 intersection A2)=3/22 exceeds P(A1)P(A2)=15/121, while the uniform conditional cutset bound 3/8 remains valid. At q=1,p=1/2, duplicating a one-edge set likewise invalidates the product (1/2>1/4); at q=p=1/2 a free one-edge graph violates an open<=p bound (2/3>1/2).
assumptions: the stated finite FK graphs and boundary partitions
ordinary physical crossing distinguished from boundary wiring
proof_or_counterexample: Enumerate all eight edge configurations for the wired path. At p=1/2 their common p factors cancel; component weights total 66 for q=3. Ordinary crossing has weight 6, wired connectivity 21, A1 weight 18, A2 weight 30 and intersection weight 9. The remaining one-edge cases follow from the explicit FK conditional formula.
remaining_gap: These are counterexamples to weakened auxiliary assumptions, not refutations of w462's correctly scoped lemmas or of C0048.
